claims: Artemis II is the first crewed mission of NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion capsule.
Artemis II is scheduled to launch no earlier than April 1, 2026.
Artemis II will carry four astronauts around the Moon to test systems for future lunar landings.
SLS provides over 8.8 million pounds of thrust.
The purpose of the Artemis II SLS rocket is to launch the crewed Orion capsule into space for a 10-day lunar flyby mission.
SLS utilizes components from the Space Shuttle program.
SLS is comparable to the Saturn V.
SLS uses two solid rocket boosters.
SLS generates 8.8 million pounds of thrust at lift-off.
Boeing built the SLS core stage.
United Launch Alliance developed the interim cryogenic propulsion system (ICPS) for SLS.
In Artemis II, after launch, the Orion spacecraft will separate.
In Artemis II, the Orion spacecraft will test systems.
Artemis II includes a Proximity Operations Demo to manually fly around the upper stage.
Artemis II will carry NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and CSA astronaut Jeremy Hansen.
